summary: Serve shared files from servers near users to reduce distance and protect the origin.
goals: Why users far from a server experience more delay
How edge servers cache static files
How cold caches and versioned names affect updates
How a CDN helps protect the origin
When to keep personal pages out of a CDN cache

steps.callout: Light takes time to travel. To reduce distance-related delay, serve content from a location closer to the user.
Images, scripts, stylesheets, and videos are often static files: the same for many users and changed infrequently.

body: A CDN (content delivery network) has edge servers in many cities. Point static files to the CDN, and users can get them from a nearby edge. London now gets images in about 10 ms. Only cache misses (amber) need to travel back to the origin in Virginia.
steps.callout: Common CDNs include Cloudflare, Fastly, Akamai, and Amazon CloudFront. You use their edge servers instead of running your own.
A CDN edge is a pull-through cache: it fetches a file from the origin when first asked, saves a copy, and serves later requests from that copy.
A long TTL (time to live) keeps files in the CDN longer and makes it faster. But users may keep seeing an old version until the cache expires or is cleared.

body: Put a fingerprint of the file contents in its name, such as logo.3f9a.png. A changed logo gets a different name, so the CDN cannot mistake it for the old file. Now the file can be cached for a year. The HTML can use a short TTL or skip caching, and point to the latest file names.
steps.callout: Build tools such as Vite and webpack can add these content fingerprints to file names.
A CDN is a cache spread across many locations. It can serve traffic spikes at the edge and reduce the load on your origin.

body: A configuration change tells the CDN to cache every page for five minutes. Bob opens his cart, and the edge saves it. Alice opens her cart a second later, and the edge sends her Bob’s cart. Pages that depend on the user must be marked Cache-Control: private (or no-store), so the CDN does not serve one person’s page to another.
steps.callout: Treat personal pages as private by default. Cache public content only when you intend to.

body: A CDN can have hundreds of edge servers. If a new file becomes popular, every edge may miss and request the same file from the origin at once. An origin shield is a cache between the edge servers and the origin. Edges ask the shield; the shield asks the origin, reducing duplicate fetches.
steps.callout: Many CDNs offer an origin shield setting. Choose one near your origin.

body:
• Distance adds delay; edge servers place content closer to users.
  • CDNs are pull-through caches: an edge fetches files from the origin when it misses.
  • Versioned file names let you cache for a long time while still publishing new versions.
  • Edges can absorb traffic spikes and reduce load on the origin.
  • Do not publicly cache personal pages; an origin shield can reduce duplicate fetches.
